text: Continuous Integration, or CI, is a software development practice where developers regularly merge their code changes into a shared central repository. Instead of waiting until the end of a project to combine everyone's work, they integrate daily or even several times a day. The core of CI revolves around automated builds. Whenever a developer submits new code, the system automatically compiles the entire project. This process is followed by running tests, which check everything from basic functions to complex interactions. The main goal is catching issues early. By testing constantly, small bugs are discovered immediately, preventing them from growing into larger, harder-to-fix problems. CI pipelines orchestrate these steps—building, testing, and reporting—smoothly, giving teams fast feedback and ensuring the software remains stable and healthy.
